high.title: BOK Expected to Hike Rates Twice to 3.0% by Year-End, KED Survey Shows
high.summary: This article appears to discuss Korean monetary policy expectations, with survey results indicating the Bank of Korea may implement two rate hikes to bring the policy rate to 3.0% by year-end. The content mentions accelerating inflation in April (fastest pace in 21 months) driven by petroleum price surges following US-Iran conflict, which is reinforcing expectations for monetary policy tightening. Deputy Governor Yoo Sang-dae's remarks reportedly jolted bond markets and heightened expectations of a policy turning point. This is highly significant for KRW/USD dynamics, bond yields, and monetary policy positioning. Rate hike expectations typically strengthen currency and push bond yields higher. The geopolitical backdrop from Middle East tensions adds complexity to the policy outlook.

high.title: Dollar-Won Pares Losses as US-Iran Ceasefire Talks Spark Military Tensions
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate closed at 1,507.20 won, down 10.00 won from the previous Seoul session close but up 2.90 won from daytime trading at 1,504.30 won. Despite growing expectations that the US and Iran are nearing a ceasefire MOU, continued military brinkmanship between the two countries triggered market caution and risk-off sentiment. The geopolitical situation is creating volatility in KRW as markets oscillate between hopes for peace (KRW strengthening) and fears of escalation (KRW weakening). This dynamic is critical for FX traders as Middle East tensions continue to be a major driver of global risk sentiment and emerging market currency performance.

high.title: Dollar-Won Holds Steady as US-Iran Ceasefire Talks Stall - Closes at 1,500.20 Won
high.summary: USD/KRW extended its decline slightly in overnight trading, closing at 1,500.20 won, down 4.10 won from the previous Seoul session and 1.00 won below the day session close of 1,501.20 won. The stalling of US-Iran ceasefire negotiations led to limited movement during the New York session. The rate has now moved meaningfully stronger for the won, falling from 1,507+ levels to the 1,500 handle, indicating reduced risk premium from geopolitical concerns. This trend suggests markets are becoming more comfortable with the Middle East situation, which is positive for risk assets and EM currencies like KRW.

medium.title: South Korean Banks' BIS Ratio Falls to 15.64% in Q1 on Currency Impact
medium.summary: Domestic banks' BIS capital ratio declined to 15.64% in Q1 from 15.83% at year-end, primarily due to increased lending assets and rising exchange rates. The decline in capital adequacy ratios, while still well above regulatory minimums, reflects the impact of KRW weakness and credit growth on bank balance sheets, which could influence monetary policy considerations.

medium.title: Bank of Korea Builds 'Project Agora' Prototype, to Participate in Live Transaction Tests
medium.summary: BOK has jointly built a 'Project Agora' prototype with BIS and other institutions for live transaction tests. This public-private initiative explores cross-border payment efficiency using tokenized bank deposits and wholesale CBDC, involving central banks from six countries and over 40 global financial institutions. This signals BOK's active participation in global payment system innovation.

medium.title: Manufacturing Sentiment Turns 'Optimistic' for First Time in 3 Years, 9 Months
medium.summary: The all-industry Composite Business Survey Index rose 4.0 points to 98.9 in May, with manufacturing sentiment shifting from pessimistic to optimistic for the first time since August 2022. This improvement in business confidence supports the case for continued economic recovery and could influence BOK policy decisions.

medium.title: US 2-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand, Yield Meets Expectations
medium.summary: US 2-year Treasury auction settled at 4.071% yield, up 25.9 bps from previous month and highest since February 2025. Bid-to-cover ratio of 2.64 showed solid demand. Rising US yields provide context for global rate expectations and KRW dynamics.

medium.title: US 5-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand - Yield Slightly Above Forecast
medium.summary: US 5-year note auction concluded with 4.182% yield, up 22.7 bps month-over-month to highest level since January 2025. Bid-to-cover ratio improved to 2.34x. Continued strength in US Treasury yields maintains pressure on Korean bond yields and influences KRW through interest rate differentials.
